messages.text:
We propose replacing the adviser, copying and audit provisions with the following wording.

**Permitted use and access.** “The Testing House may use the drawings and CAD geometry solely to prepare for, conduct and report on the agreed actuator vibration tests. Access is limited to test personnel named in a list agreed in writing by both parties. The parties may approve additions or substitutions by email before access begins. Each listed person must be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The Testing House is responsible for their compliance. Neither the drawings nor geometry derived from them may be reused for another project or used to develop a competing product.”

**Working copies and fixtures.** “The Testing House may make the working copies reasonably needed for the tests. It must encrypt digital copies in storage and in transit. It may extract the minimum geometry needed to design and fabricate test fixtures and may use those fixtures only for the agreed tests. Any external fixture maker requiring access to that geometry is subject to the same named-person approval and confidentiality requirements.”

**Destruction and verification.** “Within 15 business days after the Design Owner accepts the test report in writing, or after the test engagement ends early, the Testing House must destroy its copies of the drawings, derivative geometry files and physical fixtures made from that geometry. It must obtain written confirmation of destruction from each approved external recipient and provide the Design Owner with a destruction certificate signed by its test lead identifying the materials destroyed, the method and the date. The Testing House may retain the final report and test measurements provided they contain no recoverable CAD geometry. If there is a specific, documented discrepancy in the certificate, the Testing House may resolve it by providing verification from a mutually agreed independent assessor. The Design Owner has no on-demand site access.”

Can your test systems and backup rotation meet the 15-business-day deletion period? If backups require longer, please propose a maximum expiry period and wording covering access and re-deletion if a backup is restored.

We can commit to the 15-business-day deadline for active files, working copies and fixtures, including those held by approved specialists. We have not verified a maximum backup rotation across all recipients. We propose a 90-calendar-day ceiling, with each recipient’s ability to meet it confirmed before it receives any geometry.

**Access attachment.** “The parties will agree by email on an access schedule identifying each recipient, its named personnel, its task and the material it may receive. The machining shop may receive an isolated extract containing only the geometry needed to fabricate the fixture. The accredited test lab may receive only the drawing extracts needed for its assigned tests. The Testing House may propose a replacement specialist or individual by email on the same terms. The Design Owner will approve or give specific reasons for objection within two business days. Access requires affirmative written approval. The Testing House will end the outgoing recipient’s access when its assignment ends and obtain its destruction confirmation within 15 business days of that date.”

**Backups.** “Only residual copies in access-restricted disaster-recovery backups may remain after the active-copy deletion deadline. They may be accessed solely for disaster recovery and must expire within 90 calendar days after the event that triggered deletion. If a backup is restored, the recipient must isolate the restored material and re-delete the drawings and derivative geometry before releasing the restored system for ordinary use. Restoration does not restart the expiry period.”

**Retention and verification.** “The Testing House may retain calibration and traceability records for two years after test completion, provided they contain no drawing extracts or recoverable geometry. The test lead’s destruction certificate will identify any residual backups by custodian and latest expiry date. The Testing House will confirm final expiry in writing within five business days after that date, based on its own records and written confirmations from external recipients. For a specific documented discrepancy, the parties will first use redacted logs and recipient confirmations. If those do not resolve it, a mutually agreed independent assessor may inspect relevant records by appointment, remotely or at an agreed location. Verification confers no right of entry to a shared customer site.”

Would you accept prior written approval for substitutions on the two-business-day response timetable, together with the initial certificate and separate backup-expiry confirmation?

Yes. The Design Owner accepts the proposed access schedule and will approve a substitution or give specific reasons for objection within two business days. The replacement may receive geometry only after affirmative written approval. We also accept the test lead’s initial destruction certificate and separate written confirmation of final backup expiry, with independent verification on the terms proposed.

Please incorporate the pre-transfer check you offered into the backup clause. “Before sharing geometry with named personnel, the Testing House must verify that its own backup systems can meet the 90-calendar-day ceiling. Before transferring geometry to an approved external recipient, it must obtain that recipient’s written confirmation that its systems can meet the same ceiling. Residual backups must remain encrypted and access-restricted until expiry.”

With that wording, we accept the three proposed clauses together with the previously proposed test-only use, equivalent written confidentiality obligations, Testing House responsibility for recipients, and prohibition on reuse to develop competing products.

Agreed. The final backup clause reads as follows.

**Backups.** “Before sharing geometry with named personnel, the Testing House must verify that its own backup systems can meet the 90-calendar-day ceiling. Before transferring geometry to an approved external recipient, it must obtain that recipient’s written confirmation that its systems can meet the same ceiling. Only residual copies in disaster-recovery backups may remain after the active-copy deletion deadline. Residual backups must remain encrypted and access-restricted until expiry. They may be accessed solely for disaster recovery and must expire within 90 calendar days after the event that triggered deletion. If a backup is restored, the recipient must isolate the restored material and re-delete the drawings and derivative geometry before releasing the restored system for ordinary use. Restoration does not restart the expiry period.”

The Testing House accepts this clause together with the agreed access schedule, substitution procedure, test-only use and working-copy provisions, confidentiality and recipient obligations, reuse prohibitions, and destruction, retention and verification terms.

The prototype batch now includes a drawing with export-restricted geometry on page 4. We propose a narrow addendum so testing that does not depend on that geometry can proceed.

**Drawing release.** “The Design Owner will supply a test copy that omits page 4 and contains no embedded or recoverable copy of its geometry. The Testing House and its approved recipients may use that copy under the agreed terms. Access approval does not authorize receipt of the page 4 geometry or extracts derived from it. If a recipient has already received the full drawing, it must isolate the file, suspend its use and notify the Design Owner promptly to arrange secure removal.”

**Reference coupon.** “The Design Owner will prepare a substitute reference coupon within two days after the parties agree in writing on the verification test. The coupon and its accompanying information must not disclose the restricted geometry. Before using the coupon for the affected vibration test, the Testing House will run the agreed verification test and provide the measured results. Use requires the Design Owner’s written acceptance against the agreed criteria.”

Please confirm whether the full drawing has reached any recipient. For verification, would a low-level vibration sweep on the intended fixture establish that the coupon is suitable? Please propose the response to measure, the frequency range, the reference for comparison and the acceptance tolerance. If a sweep would miss a condition that matters to the affected test, please propose a check for that condition.

We accept the drawing-release clause. We have not yet confirmed whether anyone received the full drawing. We will check our transfer records and obtain written confirmations from the shop and lab. If we identify a transfer, we will isolate the file or instruct the recipient to do so, suspend its use and notify you promptly to arrange secure removal.

**Coupon and fixture custody.** The shop has already cut stock for the original fixture. We propose holding that stock pending release of a tolerance table. Please supply the coupon directly to our test lead, who will log receipt, retain custody at the Testing House and return it to you after the affected test or on early termination. Our lead will measure the coupon against the fixture-interface tolerances you specify. The shop will receive only the resulting tolerance table, after you confirm in writing that it may be released and contains no restricted geometry or extracts. The shop may finish the existing stock if it meets those tolerances. The coupon stays at the Testing House.

**Verification and signoff.** We propose a low-level sweep on the intended fixture in each axis used for the affected test, from the lower to the upper frequency in the agreed test profile. We would measure acceleration at the coupon response point and at the fixture control point, then compare their ratio across the sweep and the frequencies of the response peaks against a reference trace you approve for the same mounting and sensor locations. We would remove and remount the coupon and repeat the sweep to check mounting repeatability. A low-level sweep alone cannot establish that the mount stays secure at full test level. If that condition matters, we propose an agreed intermediate-level hold with a fixture-slip check before proceeding to full level.

Please specify the numerical band endpoints, reference trace, permitted deviations in response ratio and peak frequency, and run-to-run repeatability limits before we run verification. If you require the hold, please also specify its level, duration and allowable slip. Our lead will sign the measurement record and submit both traces and any hold results. The affected test will start only after your written acceptance against those criteria.

**Schedule.** We propose allowing two calendar days from written agreement on verification for you to prepare the coupon and extending the affected test milestone by the same two days. Please confirm the delivery date to our test lead and the revised milestone when we agree the criteria. If delivery or written signoff takes longer, we will agree a revised date for the affected test. Unaffected tests can proceed on the released drawing.

We accept direct delivery to your named test lead, logged custody at the Testing House and return of the coupon after the affected test or on early termination. The shop may hold the cut stock. It may resume machining once we have cleared the tolerance table in writing and confirmed that the stock is suitable for use without disclosing the page 4 geometry. Please include in your transfer check which drawing revision or extract the shop used to cut the stock, and send us the outcome of the shop and lab checks even if neither received the full drawing.

We accept the proposed sweep in each test axis and the repeat sweep after remounting. Please send the applicable test profile and revision, the proposed mounting and sensor locations, and any candidate reference trace with its measurement uncertainty. We need those inputs to set numerical limits. Our project engineer will use them to prepare a verification sheet specifying the band endpoints, approved reference trace, response-ratio and peak-frequency tolerances, and run-to-run limits. The sheet will also state whether an intermediate hold is required and, if so, its level, duration and allowable slip. Please use only released material in this exchange.

We propose adding this wording to the signoff provision. “Both parties must approve the verification sheet in writing before verification begins. The test lead will submit the signed measurement record, both sweep traces for each axis and any required hold results. The affected test may begin only after the Design Owner confirms in writing that the results meet the agreed criteria.”

We accept two calendar days from written agreement on the verification sheet to prepare the coupon and a two-calendar-day extension of the affected milestone. At that agreement, we will confirm the delivery date with your test lead and record the revised milestone. If delivery or signoff takes longer, we will agree a new date for the affected test. Unaffected tests may proceed on the released drawing.

We accept the proposed signoff wording, coupon custody terms and two-calendar-day extension. When both parties approve the verification sheet in writing, we will record the coupon delivery date and revised milestone. Our test lead will submit the signed measurement record, both sweep traces for each axis and any required hold results. We will start the affected test only after your written confirmation that the results meet the agreed criteria. If delivery or signoff takes longer, we will agree a new date. Unaffected tests may proceed on the released drawing.

The transfer check is pending. We will report the shop and lab findings in writing, including negative findings, and identify the drawing revision or extract the shop used to cut the stock. If we cannot establish its source, we will flag that explicitly. The stock will remain on hold until you clear the tolerance table and confirm the stock’s suitability in writing.

For the verification sheet, we will send the applicable released test profile and revision, the proposed mounting and sensor locations, and any available released reference trace with its measurement uncertainty. If we lack a suitable trace or its uncertainty, we will identify that gap so both parties can agree on the reference before approving the sheet.
